source: Wright Field Eng-47-1749-A, section V.D and Figures 6-7

figure6RateAxis.basis: Approximate local rate axis read against 0 and 4000 ft/min, with broad boxes around the faired low-blower climb trace.

configuration: Wing racks fitted, gear and flaps up, auto-rich, automatic oil and coolant shutters. Report data reduced to NACA standard conditions.
ratingNote: 67/75 inHg identify the commanded test schedule. Beyond its critical altitude the branch follows the falling full-throttle curve. They are not claims of 75 inHg actually held at 4000-12000 ft.
powerSource: p51-climb-state-reconstruction.json, Figure 7. Chart-assigned Packard BHP, not torque.

separateSources.source: AAF Proving Ground Command, Eglin, 7 July 1944, P-51B-15 43-24755/57/75
separateSources.finding: Independent V-1650-7 specimens. 75-inHg climb to 30000 ft about one minute faster than 67 inHg. Reset aneroid shifted at about 7500 ft, flights with full military load and no standard-temperature reduction. Aggregate time retained as a qualitative cross-check, not an absolute-rate or power calibration target.

separateSources.source: North American Aviation, Preliminary Results of Performance Tests on a P-51B Airplane with 44-1 Fuel, 25 April 1944
separateSources.finding: P-51B-5-NA V-1650-7, rates corrected to 8460 lb. Published low-blower rates 4300-4370 ft/min at 6500 ft and 67 inHg, 4650-4670 at 3500 ft and 75 inHg. TAS and installed torque for those summary states unavailable. Distinct mass and installation; not pooled.
9205 lb takeoff, V-1650-3, 3000 rpm, automatic shutters. Reports climb BHP from charts and shutter positions, with documented mixture inconsistency. No matched V-1650-7 propulsion check.
